MANILA, Philippines – The company originally owned by Vice President Sara Duterte’s husband, Mans Carpio, came under scrutiny on the 45th day of the impeachment trial, with questions emerging over its actual workforce.
The defense team’s witness, Trade Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo, said on Friday, November 20, that Cale88 had 201 employees as of 2024, based on Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) records.
The figure contrasts with its filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, which indicated that it had no “rank-and-file” employees and no “manpower complement” in 2024.
Rodolfo said DTI records also showed that the company declared 115 direct laborers and three indirect workers the previous year, with labor expenses amounting to P3.5 million.
Prosecution spokesman Zia Alonto Adiong, at a press conference, suggested that the company may be violating labor laws because of the poossibly extremely low wages.

“If we sum it up, and divide P3.1 million by 115 employees, annually, each one receives P27,066. Divide that by 12 months, and it shows each employee is paid P2,255 monthly. That’s about P75 per day. This is way below the annual wage order for Region XI,” Adiong said.

blocks.text: Senator Raffy Tulfo asked how the Board of Investments made sure that Cale88’s declarations were truthful.
“That is what they submitted, notarized. That is compared with the audited financial statement,” Rodolfo said.
He added that they can check a company’s manpower records deeper if they avail of corporate income tax exemptions.
“There is a requirement there for a certificate of good standing from SSS. Included in what SSS submits is a master list of those whose contributions are being paid,” Rodolfo said.
“Maybe that’s why they are not availing of tax holiday so they don’t have to give those documents. Therefore, they may not have those many employees,” Tulfo said.
Rodolfo confirmed that Cale88 did not apply for incentives such as VAT zero-rating, but added that he did not know why, despite their importance to exporting businesses. – Rappler.com
